anatomy.intro: Four structures that explain the form of golden ball cactus.

parts.function: The folded stem surface can accommodate changes in stored water.
parts.label: Rib

parts.function: Repeated cushions along the ribs bear the spines.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: Fine spines screen and defend the green stem beneath.
parts.label: Golden spines

parts.function: A side shoot can gradually turn a single column into a clump.
parts.label: Basal offset

flowers.text: RHS describes lemon-yellow, bowl-shaped flowers about 4–5 cm across. They rise above the spine coat on established plants, making a striking contrast between the soft-looking gold body and bright open flowers.

growth.note: Look for gradual changes in shape; indoor light and growing conditions affect the pace.

stages.text: A young stem starts with a rounded outline.
stages.title: Golden globe

stages.text: The body extends upward while retaining its many narrow ribs.
stages.title: Lengthening column

stages.text: Offsets can gather around the base of a flowering-sized column.
stages.title: Older clump

habitat.text: This species is native to Rio Grande do Sul in southern Brazil. Kew places it in seasonally dry tropical vegetation. The golden covering is a dense layer of slender spines over a green stem: a globe when young, becoming a column with age, sometimes accompanied by offsets.

lookalikes.name: Woolly Espostoa
lookalikes.text: Espostoa's white wool conceals sharper projecting spines; this Parodia has a visibly golden bristly coat.

mature.text: RHS describes columns reaching about 60 cm, either alone or in clusters. A small pot-bound globe therefore represents an early form, rather than a permanently spherical species.

milestones.text: Purchased at Carlsons' Greenhouse in a 4-inch individual pot.
milestones.title: Joined the collection

nameStory.text: Kew currently records the name as Parodia lenninghausii, published in 2010, and traces its basionym Pilocereus lenninghausii to 1896.
